common: How this game works for these rules: the AI and players change the world with Flecs Script, declarative data that the game's own engine interprets. It never downloads native code. Stores that review AI features expect content filtering, in-app reporting and blocking, and disclosure of any third-party AI. Console rules are under NDA, so their verdicts stay open until we are in their programmes.

stores.name: Android XR
stores.summary: Google's headset platform. It is Google Play: the same Play Console account, with a mobile or a dedicated XR track.

fit.verdict: Allowed with conditions, same as Google Play.
fit.detail: Device and Network Abuse policy: no downloaded executable code (dex, JAR, .so); interpreted languages loaded at runtime "must not allow potential violations of Google Play policies". Flecs Script is interpreted data, so it fits if what it makes stays within policy. The AI-Generated Content policy needs in-app reporting or flagging without leaving the app, and prohibits some content.

fit.verdict: Allowed with conditions: no rule against runtime scripts or generative AI was found.
fit.detail: Content generated or recommended by the app must meet Meta's Content Guidelines, and user content falls under the Code of Conduct for Virtual Experiences, with a way to report it. Age groups are self-certified for each submission and update. AI-specific rules were not found and are unverified.

stores.name: Apple App Store
stores.summary: iPhone, iPad, Mac App Store and Apple Vision Pro (visionOS), all through App Store Connect.

fit.verdict: Allowed with conditions, and the riskiest of the open stores for runtime scripts.
fit.detail: Guideline 2.5.2: apps "may not download, install, or execute code which introduces or changes features". Flecs Script made by the AI at runtime has to be argued as content inside the app's own sandbox: declarative data, no native APIs, no new app features. 4.7 (mini apps, chatbots) asks for filtering, reporting and blocking, and age gating. 1.2 asks AI content creation apps for filters, reports, blocking and contact details. 5.1.2(i) needs explicit permission before sharing data with third-party AI. Expect questions from App Review; nothing here is certain.

facts.label: Developer account
facts.value: Apple Developer Program, about 99 USD a year (check the current fee).

facts.label: Devices
facts.value: A Mac with Xcode for every Apple build; visionOS needs an Apple-silicon Mac. Test iPhone/iPad strongly advised; Vision Pro has a simulator.

facts.label: Review
facts.value: Human App Review for every build and update in App Store Connect.

facts.label: Unity
facts.value: iOS and macOS are supported in the normal editor. visionOS needs Unity Pro, Enterprise or Industry.

facts.label: AI content
facts.value: Filtering, report and block tools, published contact details, third-party AI disclosure and consent, age rating from the App Store Connect questionnaire.
